title: Production of a Versatile Pan-DENV NS5 Polyclonal Antibody and Structural Epitope Analysis of Immunogen Performance
abstract: Background: Dengue is a major mosquito-borne viral disease worldwide, with approximately 400 million infections reported annually and no fully effective antiviral treatments available. The non-structural protein NS5 is a promising antiviral target due to its critical role in viral RNA replication and host interactions. Although commercial monoclonal and polyclonal anti-NS5 antibodies are available, none were found to combine broad reactivity against all four dengue virus serotypes with suitability for Western Blot (WB), Immunofluorescence (IF), and Immunoprecipitation (IP) assays. This study aimed to develop and functionally characterize a versatile polyclonal antibody targeting a conserved region of DENV NS5 for immunodetection applications. Methods: Conserved recombinant regions from the methyltransferase (MTase) and RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp) domains of DENV2 NS5 were expressed in Escherichia coli and used as immunogens in a murine model. Results: Both recombinant proteins exhibited predicted antigenic potential, but only the anti-NS5-RdRp antibody efficiently recognized native NS5 in infected cells. The resulting antibody detected NS5 from all four dengue serotypes in WB, with lower nonspecific background than a widely used commercial antibody. In addition, it proved effective in IF and IP assays in DENV1- and DENV2-infected cells, enabling co-immuno-precipitation of NS3, a known NS5 interactor. Retrospective structural epitope analyses suggested that the RdRp immunogen contained surface-accessible conformational features more compatible with antibody recognition in the native protein context. Conclusion: These findings identify the anti-NS5-RdRp antibody as a valuable tool for dengue research and illustrate how structural epitope analyses can provide insights into differences in immunogen performance

title_zh: 多功能泛 DENV NS5 多克隆抗体的生产和免疫原性能的结构表位分析
source_body_en: Background: Dengue is a major mosquito-borne viral disease worldwide, with approximately 400 million infections reported annually and no fully effective antiviral treatments available. The non-structural protein NS5 is a promising antiviral target due to its critical role in viral RNA replication and host interactions. Although commercial monoclonal and polyclonal anti-NS5 antibodies are available, none were found to combine broad reactivity against all four dengue virus serotypes with suitability for Western Blot (WB), Immunofluorescence (IF), and Immunoprecipitation (IP) assays. This study aimed to develop and functionally characterize a versatile polyclonal antibody targeting a conserved region of DENV NS5 for immunodetection applications. Methods: Conserved recombinant regions from the methyltransferase (MTase) and RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp) domains of DENV2 NS5 were expressed in Escherichia coli and used as immunogens in a murine model. Results: Both recombinant proteins exhibited predicted antigenic potential, but only the anti-NS5-RdRp antibody efficiently recognized native NS5 in infected cells. The resulting antibody detected NS5 from all four dengue serotypes in WB, with lower nonspecific background than a widely used commercial antibody. In addition, it proved effective in IF and IP assays in DENV1- and DENV2-infected cells, enabling co-immuno-precipitation of NS3, a known NS5 interactor. Retrospective structural epitope analyses suggested that the RdRp immunogen contained surface-accessible conformational features more compatible with antibody recognition in the native protein context. Conclusion: These findings identify the anti-NS5-RdRp antibody as a valuable tool for dengue research and illustrate how structural epitope analyses can provide insights into differences in immunogen performance

title: Análise do acompanhamento e diagnóstico de gestantes e recém-nascidos com suspeita de infecção por Zika vírus no Espírito Santo, Brasil: acertos e pontos de melhoria para futuras epidemias
abstract: Zika virus (ZIKV) infection gained prominence in 2015 following a marked increase in cases of microcephaly and other congenital abnormalities among newborns of women infected during pregnancy, ultimately leading to the recognition of Congenital Zika Syndrome (CZS). This longitudinal descriptive study aimed to analyze changes in epidemiological surveillance, diagnostic methods, and the classification of suspected CZS cases in the state of Espírito Santo, Brazil, using data from the unified RESP-Microcephaly/DATASUS database from 2015 to 2024. Case incidence and temporal trends were analyzed, as well as associations between maternal infection, vertical transmission, clinical manifestations, diagnostic methods, and neonatal outcomes, using chi-square tests, odds ratios (OR), and binomial logistic regression. A total of 851 suspected cases of ZIKV infection during pregnancy were analyzed, according to data availability for each variable. The number of investigated cases peaked in 2016, followed by a progressive decline in notifications in subsequent years. Newborns of mothers with confirmed ZIKV infection had higher odds of CZS confirmation (OR = 5.1; 95% CI: 2.28–11.4; *p* < 0.001), supporting the occurrence of vertical transmission. Maternal clinical manifestations were significantly associated with confirmed infection, whereas the clinical characteristics evaluated in newborns were not. Among newborns, only IgM serology and PCR were significantly associated with diagnosis, although these were the least frequently used tests, whereas imaging examinations, which were more commonly performed, showed no significant association with case confirmation. In addition, maternal signs and symptoms showed greater diagnostic discrimination than the clinical characteristics assessed in newborns. These findings suggest limitations in the diagnostic strategy adopted for newborns and a possible underestimation of infection incidence, highlighting the need to strengthen prenatal follow-up, expand access to more informative laboratory diagnostic methods, and improve epidemiological investigation, thereby contributing to more effective responses to future epidemics.

title: Insights into Inhibitory Effects of Lapachol against Zika Virus
abstract: Abstract The reemergence of Zika virus (ZIKV) in 2015 and its association with severe neurological manifestations highlighted the urgent need for effective antiviral therapies, which, despite extensive efforts, remain unavailable. Lapachol, a 1,4-naphthoquinone compound abundant in Brazilian plant species, seems to be a promising candidate as an antiviral agent since its activity against other RNA viruses, as well as other human pathogens, including reported activity against Epstein–Barr virus and inhibition of herpes simplex virus type 1 by a lapachol-derived compound. Here, we investigated the activity of lapachol in inhibiting ZIKV replication by employing the wild-type strain ZIKVPE243. Lapachol exhibited potent inhibition of ZIKV with an EC50 of 3 μM and selectivity index of 50. Mechanistic assays suggest that its main action is exerted through postentry inhibition of viral replication, possibly through the blockage of the catalytic sites of NS2B-NS3 protease and NS5 polymerase. Biochemical enzymatic assays confirmed that lapachol inhibits NS2B-NS3 protease and NS5 polymerase activities, being complemented by molecular docking analyses. A protective effect was noted when cells were treated prior to infection, and lapachol was found to induce ROS formation in vitro, indicating that several antiviral mechanisms may be involved, including the initiation of an oxidative stress response that can affect viral particles. Overall, these findings shed light on the potential of lapachol to be used for the development of ZIKV inhibitors, especially targeting postentry stages of virus replication.
authors: Maria Eduarda Trevisan Aguillar da Silva
Nathalya Cristina de Moraes Roso Mesquita

title: Hábitos saludables y educación sanitaria para la prevención de enfermedades infecciosas
abstract: Las enfermedades infecciosas conforman una carga persistente en Ecuador, sostenida por determinantes sociales, ambientales y conductuales que trascienden el origen biológico de cada patología. Este artículo analizó la relación entre hábitos saludables, educación sanitaria y prevención de enfermedades infecciosas mediante una revisión bibliográfica narrativa con búsqueda segmentada por eje temático. El dengue representó el 95,2% de los ingresos hospitalarios por enfermedades vectoriales entre 2015 y 2022 y el 91,3% de los cuadros arbovirales registrados en 36 años. La prevalencia de Entamoeba histolytica superó el 92% en una comunidad indígena sin condiciones adecuadas de saneamiento. Las intervenciones educativas sobre higiene mostraron mejoras relevantes en el conocimiento y la práctica, mientras que la vacunación infantil evidenció barreras asociadas con la disponibilidad de biológicos y la distancia geográfica. En Jipijapa, los factores ambientales y de estilo de vida mostraron un peso superior al de los factores biológicos. Asimismo, los talleres comunitarios apoyados por herramientas digitales incrementaron los conocimientos preventivos y redujeron infecciones respiratorias. Los hallazgos indican que la prevención efectiva requiere articular educación sanitaria, acceso a recursos, participación comunitaria y continuidad institucional.

title: Pelatihan Pengembangan Spray Anti Nyamuk Ekstrak Kemangi dan Kayu Putih sebagai Media Edukasi Literasi Kesehatan Siswa
abstract: Environmentally-based diseases such as dengue fever remain a public health problem in tropical regions. This study aimed to determine the health literacy levels of students at Muaro Jambi State High School 8 after participating in a training program based on a participatory and eco-health approach through the development of a mosquito repellent spray made from basil and eucalyptus extracts. The study employed a single-group design involving 40 students divided into several groups. The series of activities comprised four stages: preparation; program implementation (eco-health education, introduction to natural ingredients, and hands-on spray-making practice); completion of a health literacy questionnaire consisting of 42 statements on a 1–4 scale; and evaluation. The evaluation results showed that the students’ health literacy level after participating in the activity fell into the “good” category, with an average score of 2.98 out of 4.00, or 74.45%. The highest achievement was in the aspect of food safety at 84.72%, followed by chemicals and the environment at 77.03%, water safety at 74.31%, and air quality at 63.08%. Based on the results of this training activity, it can be concluded that training on the development of natural-ingredient-based sprays can provide contextual learning experiences and serve as an educational tool for students’ health literacy by integrating aspects of health, the environment, and the use of natural ingredients.

Email: anikethreddygaddam@gmail.com ABSTRACT Background: Immune thrombocytopenic purpura (ITP) is an acquired immune-mediated disorder characterized by isolated thrombocytopenia and increased bleeding risk. Dengue fever is a recognized trigger for secondary ITP. Case Presentation: A 42-year-old female presented with gum bleeding and oral purpura. She had a history of dengue fever three months earlier. Evaluation revealed severe thrombocytopenia, anemia, elevated LDH, and reactive lymphocytes. Autoimmune and infectious workup was negative. Management: The patient received corticosteroids, supportive transfusions, and symptomatic management. Secondary ITP following dengue infection was considered the most probable diagnosis. Conclusion: Persistent thrombocytopenia after dengue should prompt evaluation for secondary ITP. Keywords: Immune thrombocytopenia; Secondary ITP; Dengue fever; Thrombocytopenia; Autoimmune hematology; Corticosteroids; Post-infectious immune disorder. How to cite this article: Elavarasan, Subramaniam SK, Gnanaprakash, Arvindraj R, Gopinath A, Kishore MS, Gaddam AR. Beyond Dengue: Secondary Immune Thrombocytopenia Presenting as Persistent Mucocutaneous Bleeding-A Case Report and Narrative Review. Int J Drug Deliv Technol. 2026;16(57s): 1299-1301. DOI: 10.25258/ijddt.16.57s.128 Source of support: Nil Conflict of interest: None INTRODUCTION Immune thrombocytopenia (ITP) is an acquired autoimmune disorder characterized by isolated thrombocytopenia resulting from increased platelet destruction and impaired platelet production. It may be primary or secondary to infections, autoimmune diseases, immunodeficiency states, and malignancies. Dengue fever is increasingly recognized as a trigger for persistent immune-mediated thrombocytopenia. This report describes a patient who developed probable secondary ITP following dengue infection and reviews current evidence regarding its epidemiology, pathogenesis, and management. CASE PRESENTATION A 42-year-old female presented with spontaneous bleeding from the gums for five days. She subsequently Beyond Dengue: Secondary Immune Thrombocytopenia Presenting as Persistent Mucocutaneous Bleeding-A Case Report and Narrative Review IJDDT, Volume 16 Issue 57s, 2026 Page 1300 developed multiple purpuric lesions over the oral mucosa. There was no history of hematuria, melena, menorrhagia, fever, rash, photosensitivity, oral ulcers, or recent drug intake. Three months prior, she had been diagnosed with dengue fever and received one unit of single donor platelets, four units of random donor platelets, and four units of fresh frozen plasma. Since recovery, she experienced intermittent gum bleeding and myalgias. On examination, pallor and oral purpura were present. There was no lymphadenopathy, edema, or hepatomegaly. Mild splenomegaly was noted. Laboratory investigations revealed: Hemoglobin: 6.1–7.2 g/dL Platelet count: 21,000–23,000/mm3 Total leukocyte count: Normal Peripheral smear: Microcytic hypochromic anemia with severe thrombocytopenia Reactive lymphocytes present LDH: 1040 U/L ANA profile: Negative Viral serology: Negative Direct Coombs test: Negative The patient received intravenous vitamin K, dexamethasone, pulse methylprednisolone, cefotaxime, proton pump inhibitor therapy, fresh frozen plasma, and packed red blood cell transfusion. Following exclusion of alternative etiologies, a diagnosis of probable secondary ITP following dengue infection was considered. NARRATIVE REVIEW Epidemiology and Clinical Presentation ITP affects approximately 2–5 individuals per 100,000 population annually. Secondary ITP accounts for nearly 20% of adult cases and may occur following viral infections including HIV, hepatitis C, Epstein-Barr virus, cytomegalovirus, and dengue fever. Clinical manifestations range from asymptomatic thrombocytopenia to severe mucocutaneous bleeding. Common features include petechiae, purpura, ecchymosis, epistaxis, gingival bleeding, and menorrhagia. Severe internal bleeding is uncommon but may occur in profound thrombocytopenia Pathophysiological Mechanisms The pathogenesis of ITP involves both humoral and cellular immune dysfunction. Key mechanisms included are-Autoantibody-mediated platelet destruction,Splenic macrophage phagocytosis of antibody-coated platelets,T-cell-mediated platelet destruction,Impaired megakaryocyte maturation and platelet production,Persistent immune activation following infections such as dengue. Dengue-associated ITP is thought to result from molecular mimicry, immune complex formation, and prolonged immune dysregulation after viral clearance. Medical Management First-Line Therapy is corticosteroids,Prednisolone: 1–2 mg/kg/day and High-dose dexamethasone: 40 mg daily for 4 days Benefits are rapid platelet recovery, they are widely available and cost effective Intravenous Immunoglobulin (IVIg) Used when:Rapid platelet increase is required,severe bleeding occurs,steroids are contraindicated Second-line treatment options for ITP include rituximab, a monoclonal antibody directed against CD20-positive B lymphocytes that reduces autoantibody production through B-cell depletion; thrombopoietin receptor agonists such as romiplostim and eltrombopag, which stimulate platelet production and are particularly effective in chronic or refractory disease; and various immunosuppressive agents including azathioprine, cyclosporine, mycophenolate mofetil, cyclophosphamide, and dapsone. Splenectomy remains an important therapeutic option for patients with chronic ITP, steroid- dependent disease, refractory thrombocytopenia, or failure of medical therapy, providing durable remission in a substantial proportion of cases. Clinical significance Secondary ITP following dengue infection is uncommon but clinically important. Persistent thrombocytopenia after recovery from dengue should not automatically be attributed to residual viral effects. Early identification of immune-mediated mechanisms allows timely initiation of immunosuppressive therapy and prevention of bleeding complications. DISCUSSION This case highlights the diagnostic challenge posed by persistent thrombocytopenia following dengue infection. The temporal association with dengue, exclusion of autoimmune and malignant causes, and presence of reactive lymphocytes support an immune-mediated process. The favorable response to corticosteroid therapy further strengthens the diagnosis of secondary ITP. Early diagnosis is essential to prevent significant bleeding complications. CLINICAL IMPLICATIONS Clinicians should maintain a high index of suspicion for secondary ITP in patients with persistent Beyond Dengue: Secondary Immune Thrombocytopenia Presenting as Persistent Mucocutaneous Bleeding-A Case Report and Narrative Review IJDDT, Volume 16 Issue 57s, 2026 Page 1301 thrombocytopenia after dengue infection. Comprehensive evaluation and timely immunosuppressive therapy may reduce morbidity and improve patient outcomes. LIMITATIONS Bone marrow examination was not performed. Long-term follow-up data were unavailable because the patient opted for discharge against medical advice. A definitive causal relationship between dengue infection and ITP therefore cannot be conclusively established. Future Perspectives Further studies are required to determine the incidence, risk factors, and optimal management strategies for post- dengue ITP. Research into immunological biomarkers may facilitate earlier diagnosis and targeted therapy. CONCLUSION Secondary ITP should be considered in patients with persistent thrombocytopenia and bleeding manifestations following dengue infection. Prompt recognition, exclusion of alternative etiologies, and appropriate immunosuppressive therapy are critical for preventing complications and improving outcomes. REFERENCES 1. It may be primary or secondary to infections, autoimmune diseases, immunodeficiency states, and malignancies. Dengue fever is increasingly recognized as a trigger for persistent immune-mediated thrombocytopenia. This report describes a patient who developed probable secondary ITP following dengue infection and reviews current evidence regarding its epidemiology, pathogenesis, and management. Persistent thrombocytopenia after recovery from dengue should not automatically be attributed to residual viral effects. analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on secondary immune thrombocytopenia (ITP) presenting as persistent mucocutaneous bleeding, specifically in the context of dengue infection. The central question is whether persistent thrombocytopenia after dengue should be attributed to residual viral effects or an immune-mediated process.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a narrative review and case report, not a systematic or meta-analysis. It includes a single case study of a patient with dengue infection who developed secondary ITP. The evidence is derived from clinical observations and laboratory findings, with no mention of databases, search dates, or eligibility criteria for study inclusion.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that secondary ITP following dengue infection is uncommon but clinically important. It emphasizes that persistent thrombocytopenia after dengue should not be automatically attributed to residual viral effects. The pathogenesis of ITP is described as involving immune dysfunction, including autoantibody-mediated platelet destruction, splenic macrophage phagocytosis, and T-cell-mediated destruction. The case supports an immune-mediated process rather than a direct viral effect.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review notes that a definitive causal relationship between dengue infection and ITP cannot be conclusively established due to the lack of long-term follow-up data. It also highlights the need for further studies to determine the incidence, risk factors, and optimal management strategies for post-dengue ITP.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review suggests that clinicians should maintain a high index of suspicion for secondary ITP in patients with persistent thrombocytopenia and bleeding manifestations following dengue infection. It recommends comprehensive evaluation and timely immunosuppressive therapy to reduce morbidity and improve patient outcomes.

analysis.summary_en: This narrative review and case report explores secondary immune thrombocytopenia (ITP) presenting as persistent mucocutaneous bleeding in the context of dengue infection. The review highlights the diagnostic challenge of distinguishing between residual viral effects and immune-mediated processes in patients with prolonged thrombocytopenia. It concludes that secondary ITP is uncommon but clinically significant, and that persistent thrombocytopenia should not be automatically attributed to the virus. The case study supports an immune-mediated etiology, and the review emphasizes the need for further research on the incidence, risk factors, and management of post-dengue ITP. Clinicians are advised to consider secondary ITP in such cases and to pursue timely immunosuppressive therapy.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述重点关注表现为持续性皮肤粘膜出血的继发性免疫性血小板减少症(ITP),特别是在登革热感染的情况下。核心问题是登革热后持续性血小板减少是否应归因于残留病毒效应或免疫介导的过程。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该评论是叙述性评论和病例报告,而不是系统分析或荟萃分析。它包括一名患有登革热感染并出现继发性 ITP 的患者的单个案例研究。证据来自临床观察和实验室结果,没有提及数据库、检索日期或研究纳入的资格标准。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 该综述得出的结论是,登革热感染后继发性 ITP 并不常见,但具有临床意义。它强调登革热后持续性血小板减少不应自动归因于残留病毒效应。ITP 的 发病机制 被描述为涉及免疫功能障碍,包括自身抗体介导的血小板破坏、脾巨噬细胞吞噬作用和 T 细胞介导的破坏。该病例支持免疫介导的过程,而不是直接的病毒效应。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 审查指出,由于缺乏长期随访数据,无法最终确定登革热感染与 ITP 之间的明确因果关系。它还强调需要进一步研究以确定登革热后 ITP 的 发病率、风险因素和最佳管理策略。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 该综述建议,对于登革热感染后出现持续性血小板减少和出血表现的患者,临床医生应对继发性 ITP 保持高度怀疑。它建议进行全面评估并及时进行免疫抑制治疗,以降低发病率并改善患者预后。

full_text: Evaluating the Efficacy of Serodiagnosis Technique of Dengue Virus Infection: An Epidemiological Study and Surveillance Analysis in Dimapur, Nagaland, India Abstract: This study assessed the serodiagnostic and epidemiological characteristics of dengue virus (DENV) infection in Dimapur, Nagaland, India. A prospective study was conducted at the Department of Microbiology, District Hospital, Dimapur, from March 2023 to February 2024. Serum samples from 7,074 patients with suspected dengue infection were screened using rapid diagnostic tests for NS1 antigen and IgM antibodies, followed by NS1 and IgM ELISA confirmation. Selected samples were analyzed by RT-PCR for DENV serotyping. ELISA confirmed dengue infection in 2,010 cases, including 1,461 NS1-positive and 549 IgM-positive samples. Cases increased during the post-monsoon period, with the highest number recorded in October. Infection was more common among males and was most frequent in individuals aged 21-30 years. Among 39 samples suitable for molecular analysis, DENV-2 was detected in 13 samples, while 10 demonstrated co-infection with DENV-1 and DENV-2. Environmental assessment identified water logging, swamps, and mosquito breeding sites as potential contributors to transmission. The findings indicate substantial dengue transmission in Dimapur, characterized by seasonal and demographic variation and circulation of multiple DENV serotypes. Strengthening timely serological diagnosis, molecular surveillance, and integrated vector-control measures, particularly during the post-monsoon season, is essential for effective dengue prevention and control. Keywords: Dengue virus, ELISA, DENV, Serotyping, Epidemiology How to Cite?: Dr. Epibeni N. Humtsoe, Dr. Brajesh Joshi, "Evaluating the Efficacy of Serodiagnosis Technique of Dengue Virus Infection: An Epidemiological Study and Surveillance Analysis in Dimapur, Nagaland, India", Volume 15 Issue 10, October 2026, International Journal of Science and Research (IJSR), Pages: 371-374, https://www.ijsr.net/getabstract.php?paperid=SR261005130123, DOI: https://dx.doi.org/10.21275/SR261005130123

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy of serodiagnosis techniques for dengue virus infection and assess its epidemiological characteristics in Dimapur, Nagaland, India, to inform public health strategies.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A prospective study was conducted at the Department of Microbiology, District Hospital, Dimapur, from March 2023 to February 2024, involving 7,074 patients with suspected dengue infection.
analysis.methods: Serum samples were screened using rapid diagnostic tests for NS1 antigen and IgM antibodies, followed by NS1 and IgM ELISA confirmation. Selected samples were analyzed by RT-PCR for DENV serotyping.
analysis.main_results: ELISA confirmed dengue infection in 2,010 cases, including 1,461 NS1-positive and 549 IgM-positive samples. Among 39 samples suitable for molecular analysis, DENV-2 was detected in 13 samples, while 10 demonstrated co-infection with DENV-1 and DENV-2.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study highlights the seasonal and demographic variation in dengue transmission and the circulation of multiple DENV serotypes, providing novel insights into the epidemiological patterns of the disease.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings emphasize the importance of timely serological diagnosis and molecular surveillance, particularly during the post-monsoon season, to enhance dengue prevention and control efforts.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's results are based on a single center and a specific time period, which may limit generalizability. However, the evidence is strong due to the use of multiple diagnostic methods and the detailed epidemiological analysis.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the serodiagnosis technique for dengue virus infection in Dimapur, Nagaland, India, through a prospective epidemiological study conducted from March 2023 to February 2024. Serum samples from 7,074 suspected dengue patients were tested using rapid diagnostic tests for NS1 antigen and IgM antibodies, followed by ELISA confirmation and RT-PCR for serotyping. The results showed that ELISA confirmed 2,010 cases, with DENV-2 detected in 13 samples and co-infection with DENV-1 and DENV-2 in 10 samples. The study identified seasonal and demographic variations in dengue transmission, with the highest cases recorded in October. It also noted that infection was more common among males and individuals aged 21-30 years. The findings suggest the need for strengthening timely serological diagnosis and molecular surveillance, especially during the post-monsoon season, to improve dengue prevention and control. The study's limitations include its focus on a single center and time period, which may affect generalizability, but the evidence is robust due to the use of multiple diagnostic methods and detailed epidemiological analysis.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在评估印度那加兰邦迪马普尔 登革病毒 感染血清诊断技术的有效性,并评估其流行病学特征,为公共卫生策略提供信息。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 2023年3月至2024年2月,迪马普尔地区医院微生物科进行了一项前瞻性研究,涉及7,074名疑似登革热感染患者。
elements_zh.methods: 使用 NS1 抗原和 IgM 抗体快速诊断测试筛选血清样本,然后进行 NS1 和 IgM ELISA 确认。通过 RT-PCR 对所选样本进行 DENV 血清分型分析。
elements_zh.main_results: ELISA 确诊 2,010 例登革热感染病例,其中 1,461 例 NS1 阳性样本和 549 例 IgM 阳性样本。在39个适合分子分析的样本中,有13个样本检测到DENV-2,而10个样本则证明DENV-1和DENV-2同时感染。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该研究强调了登革热 传播 的季节性和人口统计变化以及多种 DENV 血清型的传播,为该疾病的流行病学模式提供了新的见解。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果强调了及时进行血清学 诊断 和分子 监测 检测对于加强登革热预防和控制工作的重要性,特别是在季风后季节。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的结果基于单一中心和特定时间段,这可能会限制普遍性。然而,由于使用了多种诊断方法和详细的流行病学分析,证据是强有力的。

abstract_zh: 评估登革病毒感染血清诊断技术的有效性:一项流行病学研究及Dimapur地区监测分析摘要:本研究评估了印度那加兰邦迪马普尔地区登革病毒(DENV)感染的血清诊断和流行病学特征。该研究于2023年3月至2024年2月在迪马普尔区医院微生物科进行前瞻性研究。研究结果表明,迪马普尔地区登革热传播显著,具有季节性和人口学特征的变化,并且存在多种DENV血清型的循环。Brajesh Joshi,《评估登革病毒感染血清诊断技术的有效性:一项流行病学研究及Dimapur地区监测分析》,第15卷第10期,2026年10月,国际科学与研究期刊(IJSR),第371-374页,https://www.ijsr.net/getabstract.php?paperid=SR261005130123,DOI:https://dx.doi.org/10.21275/SR261005130123。对7,074例疑似登革热感染患者的血清样本进行了NS1抗原和IgM抗体的快速诊断测试,并通过NS1和IgM ELISA进行确认。选定的样本通过RT-PCR进行DENV血清型分析。ELISA确认了2,010例登革热感染病例,包括1,461例NS1阳性样本和549例IgM阳性样本。病例数在雨季后增加,10月记录的病例数最高。感染在男性中更为常见,且在21-30岁人群中最为普遍。在39份适合分子分析的样本中,检测到13份为DENV-2,另外10份同时感染了DENV-1和DENV-2。环境评估发现积水、沼泽和蚊虫繁殖地可能是传播的潜在因素。

full_text: ABSTRACTThe Amapa State, Brazil, in the Amazon region and bordering French Guiana, is a strategic sentinel location for infectious disease surveillance. Ecological pressures such as deforestation, artisanal gold mining, and high human mobility contribute to complex transmission dynamics of arboviruses, bacterial infections, and other pathogens. This study aims to characterize the etiologies of acute febrile illness (AFI) reported in Amapa State in 2018-2020, focusing on arbovirus circulation, bacterial contributions, and emerging pathogens. A retrospective analysis was carried out with 727 AFI cases. Laboratory diagnoses were established using molecular and serological assays, with systematic testing for different pathogens. Definitive diagnoses were obtained in 185 individuals (25.4%), yielding 209 positive results and including 23 cases of co-infection. Dengue virus was the predominant etiological agent (n=109, 52%), followed by leptospirosis (n=20, 9.5%), chikungunya virus (n=16, 7.6%), parvovirus B19 (n=16, 7.6%), measles (n=15, 7.1%), zika virus (n=10, 4.8%), mayaro virus (n=1,0.5%), and other bacterial infections (n=5, 2.4%). Isolated cases of hepatitis A and B, malaria, SARS-CoV-2, enterovirus, and acute Chagas disease were also identified. No hepatitis E virus or oropouche cases were detected. Dengue virus was the leading cause of AFI. Leptospirosis, chikungunya virus, and parvovirus B19 were other prevalent and often underrecognized contributors. The detection of additional viruses highlights Amapa State as a potential zone of “silent expansion” for emerging arboviruses. Co-detection of multiple pathogens underscores diagnostic complexity in regions with overlapping transmission. Strengthening surveillance, expanding laboratory capacity, and prioritizing differential diagnostics are essential to capture epidemiological dynamics and guide public health interventions.KEYWORDS: Dengue, Leptospirosis, Arbovirus infections, Chikungunya fever, Parvovirus B19 MATERIAL AND METHODSStudy design and populationAn observational, cross-sectional, retrospective, and descriptive study was conducted using a convenience sample. Serum specimens were collected from patients presenting with AFI during routine diagnostic procedures in public health laboratories. Samples from 727 individuals, collected in 2018 (n = 20), 2019 (n = 581), and 2020 (n = 126), were analyzed.This study aims to find the potential etiologies of viral and other infections in AFI cases reported from 2018 to 2022 in the Amazon region of Amapa State, Brazil. AFI, with a fever duration cutoff of 2-7 day from onset, was chosen as the inclusion criterion.Laboratory proceduresSpecimens were initially processed at the Central Public Health Laboratory of Amapa State (LACEN-AP) following routine diagnostic protocols, including arbovirus screening when clinically indicated. Additional tests, such as serology and polymerase chain reaction (PCR) for other pathogens, were performed at the discretion of attending physicians, with results recorded on GAL. Confirmatory local methods included enzyme linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) for immunoglobulin M (IgM) and NS1 (the latter exclusively for dengue), electrochemiluminescence, reverse transcription PCR (RT-PCR), and sequencing; for bacterial and fungal infections, ELISA for leptospirosis and blood, urine, and stool cultures were performed; whereas parasitic infections were confirmed using thick blood smears, the Strout test, electrochemiluminescence, and immunochromatographic tests.After initial processing, samples were stored at −20 °C and shipped to the Virology Laboratory of the Institute of Tropical Medicine of Sao Paulo, Faculty of Medicine, University of Sao Paulo (LV-IMT-FMUSP, LIM-52), in which they were preserved at −80 °C until further testing.Molecular screeningAt LV-IMT-FMUSP, samples underwent real-time PCR assays targeting viral agents. The screening included assays for Pan-Orthoflavivirus and Pan-Alphavirus. The following viral agents were tested: Flaviviruses, Alphaviruses, Orthobunyaviruses: yellow fever 8 , dengue, zika, chikungunya, mayaro, and oropouche viruses 9 .Genus Orthoflavivirus 10 : Japanese encephalitis, Russian spring-summer encephalitis, tick-borne encephalitis, Usutu, West Nile, and Saint Louis encephalitis viruses.Genus Alphavirus 11 : Ross River, O’nyong-nyong, Sindbis, Barmah Forest, Eastern equine encephalitis, Western equine encephalitis, and Venezuelan equine encephalitis viruses. Additional real-time PCR assays included pathogens with overlapping clinical presentations, such as enterovirus 12 , parvovirus B19 13 , hepatitis E virus (HEV) 14 , and Leptospira spp 15 .GALIn this study, diagnostic test results from LACEN-AP were retrieved via GAL.GAL, the national computerized system, was designed to manage and monitor laboratory routines within the National Public Health Laboratory Network. It is managed by the Ministry of Health via the General Coordination of Public Health Laboratories and tracks the flow of biological samples from collection to final diagnosis, standardizing results and providing real-time data for the surveillance of high-priority and compulsory notification diseases.SINANSINAN, the primary national surveillance database managed by the Brazilian Ministry of Health, is a decentralized system fed by the mandatory notification of diseases and conditions in the National Compulsory Notification List.SINAN provides high-resolution microdata (individual-level records) that include clinical and demographic variables (age, sex, pregnancy status, municipality of residence, reported condition, date of symptom onset, and clinical manifestations), diagnostic test results, among others.Integration of dataClinical and demographic variables (age, sex, municipality of residence, reported condition, date of symptom onset, and clinical manifestations) were combined with GAL laboratory results. Using this integrated dataset, data analysis was strictly descriptive, focusing on characterizing the reported cases.For the diagnostic tests either at LACEN or IMT, samples were classified as positive if they were reactive in at least one assay.Statistical analysisContinuous variables are shown as medians and interquartile ranges (IQR), and categorical ones, as frequencies. Subgroup pairwise comparisons were performed via the Pearson’s chi-square or Fisher’s exact tests. Correlation between monthly cases and NASA POWER precipitation data was assessed using Spearman’s rank test. The Benjamini-Hochberg procedure was applied to control the false discovery rate across multiple comparisons. Spatial distribution maps were generated using the geobr, sf, and ggplot2 packages. Statistical significance was set at p < 0.05, using R(version 4.4.0) via RStudio. Serum specimens were collected from patients presenting with AFI during routine diagnostic procedures in public health laboratories. AFI, with a fever duration cutoff of 2-7 day from onset, was chosen as the inclusion criterion. Regarding age, the female sex presented a median age of 28 years (interquartile range : 15-45), with values ranging from0.008 to 90 years. For males, the median age was 26 years (IQR: 12-42), ranging from 0.17 to 88 years. Fever was followed by headache, myalgia, low back pain, nausea, and vomiting. Other manifestations included rash, retro-orbital pain, arthritis, arthralgia, conjunctivitis, and petechiae, with laboratory findings of leukopenia. Chronic comorbidities included systemic arterial hypertension, diabetes mellitus, and chronic kidney disease. Autoimmune diseases and isolated cases of hematological, hepatic, and peptic disorders also occurred.Of the 727 notifications, 585 (80.5%) had arbovirus infection as the initial diagnostic hypothesis—predominantly dengue, followed by chikungunya, zika, and yellow fever. The remaining 142 individuals (19.5%) presented suspicions of other conditions, including Chagas disease, pertussis, COVID-19, diphtheria, Q fever, viral hepatitis, visceral leishmaniasis, leptospirosis, rubella, measles, and toxoplasmosis.LACEN/AP performed 1,239 diagnostic tests, with 195 positive results (15.7%). Dengue was the most frequent diagnosis: 109 cases out of 650 tests (16.8%). Other notable findings included leptospirosis (20/98; 20.4%), chikungunya (16/86; 18.6%), and measles (15/53; 28.3%).Remaining positive cases involved zika (9/62; 14.5%), parvovirus B19 (6/21; 28.6%). Other positive tests for other pathogens were bacterial infections (5/17; 29.4%), Chagas disease (1/80; 1.3%), malaria (2/80; 2.5%), CMV (1/33; 3.0%), hepatitis A (2/24; 8.3%); hepatitis B (1/20; 5.0%), COVID-19 (2/4; 50.0%), influenza virus (1/2; 50%), fungal (1/1; 100%), and arbovirus screening (4/8, 50.0%).At LV-IMTFMUSP, molecular surveillance involved testing 727 individuals by RT-PCR, depending on sample availability. Samples from 727 individuals, collected in 2018 (n = 20), 2019 (n = 581), and 2020 (n = 126), were analyzed.This study aims to find the potential etiologies of viral and other infections in AFI cases reported from 2018 to 2022 in the Amazon region of Amapa State, Brazil. AFI, with a fever duration cutoff of 2-7 day from onset, was chosen as the inclusion criterion.

full_text_sections.discussion: DISCUSSIONThis study investigated the etiologies of AFI cases reported in Amapa State from 2018 to 2022. Of 727 evaluated individuals, definitive diagnoses established 185 cases (25.4%), including 23 cases of co-infection.Our findings are in line with previous regional studies. Dengue remains the predominant AFI etiological agent in Latin America, with chikungunya and zika showing an increased prevalence. Leptospirosis, though often overlooked, represents a prevalent bacterial contributor1,16.Notably, this study found one case of mayaro virus infection, consistent with its rare occurrence in Amapa State (six confirmed cases nationwide in 2015-2025) 17 . Following systematic PCR testing, no individual in our cohort was positive for Oropouche virus disease, despite epidemiological data (2015-2025) reporting 16,571 cases nationwide, including 218 in Amapa State. A recent increase in its detection (2023-2024) likely reflects greater diagnostic capacity and active case-finding 17 . These results suggest Amapa State may represent a zone of “silent expansion” for Oropouche virus disease, in which overlapping arbovirus transmission obscures true disease burden. Strengthening surveillance, expanding laboratory capacity, and prioritizing differential diagnostics are essential to capture epidemiological dynamics and guide interventions. While multiplex syndromic panels are ideal, widespread molecular testing faces strict budget and logistical constraints within the public health system in Amapa State. A more sustainable solution could be a tiered “reflex testing” cascade at LACEN-AP. Under this protocol, a negative molecular result for primary arboviruses (dengue/zika/chikungunya) would automatically trigger reflex testing for leptospirosis and parvovirus B19 using the original biological sample. This flow could optimize laboratory resources, cut costs, and bypass initial clinical triage blind spots without requiring secondary patient appointments. Lessons from the Amazon highlight the global importance of integrated arbovirus surveillance in regions with overlapping transmission.The fact that 80.5% of initial hypotheses were generically classified as suspected arboviruses exposes a profound “dengue-centric” bias. Because the early symptoms of dengue, parvovirus B19, and leptospirosis overlap almost entirely, physical triage alone is insufficient. To address this, the regional health system must implement targeted continuing medical education focusing on broad syndromic classifications—such as “acute exanthematous febrile syndrome”—rather than single-pathogen guessing. Furthermore, standard patient intake forms should mandate structured epidemiological risk questions regarding recent floodwater exposure (leptospirosis), mining or forest exposure (malaria/arboviruses), and artisanal acai consumption (acute Chagas disease) to guide clinical suspicion before laboratory results are available.Leptospirosis remains a critical public health challenge in Amapa State linked to seasonal flooding, precarious sanitation, and transmission in wetland and stilt-house communities 18 , 19 . Despite its prevalence, underreporting persists due to symptomatic overlap with malaria and dengue 20 . Our finding that Leptospira spp. was the second most prevalent confirmed pathogen underscores its critical standing in the regional etiology of AFI. Unlike arboviral infections, which only require supportive care, leptospirosis demands timely antibiotic therapy to prevent severe, potentially fatal complications such as Weil’s disease or pulmonary hemorrhage syndrome. Relying entirely on early clinical differentiation or waiting days for laboratory confirmation in highly endemic zones often results in catastrophic therapeutic delays. Therefore, in areas with high dengue and leptospirosis co-endemicity, clinical protocols must explicitly support the initiation of empirical antibiotic treatment (such as doxycycline or amoxicillin) for patients presenting with severe febrile syndromes and clear epidemiological risk factors, prioritizing clinical survival over definitive laboratory timelines.Parvovirus B19 occurred in 16 cases (7.6%), representing a notable proportion of AFI diagnoses. Its clinical recognition remains challenging as its early symptoms closely mimic arboviruses such as dengue, Zika, and chikungunya. In tropical regions, B19V is often misdiagnosed as dengue due to overlapping presentations of fever, headache, and rash 21 , 22 . The post-pandemic resurgence of B19V in 2024-2025 marked a significant epidemiological shift driven by an “immunity gap” in pediatric populations. IgM positivity peaked at ~40% in children aged 5-9 years and ~10% in adults, complicating AFI differential diagnosis 23 .Of the 727 investigated individuals, viral hepatitis was suspected in 10 cases (1.4%), with three confirmed cases of hepatitis A and B (1.4%). No HEV cases were identified despite evidence that HEV genotype 3 is a zoonotic pathogen of concern in Brazil 24 , 25 .Meta-analyses estimate anti-HEV IgG seroprevalence at ~6% nationally, with regional variations: ~3% in the Amazon and up to 14.2% in rural Rondônia 26 - 28 . Diagnostic invisibility remains a major challenge as public health screening routinely ignores HEV testing, particularly in vulnerable Amazonian populations. Overlapping clinical presentations with hepatitis b and d further obscure HEV detection, suggesting that some acute hepatitis cases of “unknown etiology” may represent undiagnosed HEV.Measles occurred in 15 cases (7.1%). Despite mass vaccination programs, Brazil lost its measles-free status in 2018 following outbreaks linked to Venezuelan migration and low vaccination coverage 29 , 30 . Although elimination status was regained in 2023-2024, new cases in Tocantins in 2025 highlight ongoing vulnerability. The porous border of Amapa State with French Guiana and high mobility of illegal gold miners create a unique epidemiological corridor sustaining measles and other infectious diseases.Malaria transmission remains a major concern in Oiapoque, one of the highest transmission zones in the Americas. Despite persistent “silent” transmission by asymptomatic carriers in mobile populations, our cohort only included two malaria cases (0.95%), reflecting the predominance of samples collected in Macapa. Epidemiological data shows a downward trend in Amapa State, with a 16.8% reduction in cases from 2024 to 2025 and an 82% decline in Macapa. Nonetheless, the Oiapoque border remains the main epidemiological challenge in the state 31 - 34 . The cohort included a case of acute Chagas disease, reflecting the specific epidemiological profile of Amapa State. From 2018 to 2022, the state remained a high-endemicity region for acute Chagas disease in the Brazilian Amazon, with oral transmission—primarily by consumption of artisanal acai and bacaba juice—emerging as the dominant route of infection 35 , 36 .A notable finding in this study was the elevated detection of multiple infectious agents. Across 727 patients, this study found 209 reactive results, with co-detection of distinct pathogens in 23 cases. Similar patterns have been reported in regions endemic for malaria and arboviruses, in which simultaneous infections are confirmed by multiple molecular assays 37 , 38 . In such contexts, potential cross-reactivity further compounds diagnostic complexity. The cross-reactivity between zika, dengue, and yellow fever serological assays, for example, is primarily attributed to the high degree of structural homology within the envelope protein in members of the Orthoflavivirus genus 39 .The seasonal transmission pattern in this study likely reflects the equatorial climate of the region, in which persistently high precipitation and elevated temperatures sustain vector breeding sites throughout the year. full_text_sections.conclusion: CONCLUSIONSThe causes of AFI in Amapa are multiple and may involve infection by more than one etiological agent. This underscores the complexity of diagnostic accuracy in regions with overlapping multiple arbovirus and bacterial transmission. The detection of rare pathogens such as Mayaro virus and acute Chagas disease reflects the unique ecological and epidemiological profile of the region. These findings reinforce the role of Amapa State as a sentinel for infectious disease surveillance as its porous borders, ecological connectivity, and high human mobility sustain transmission corridors. Strengthening laboratory capacity, integrating differential diagnostics, and expanding surveillance systems are essential to capture the true burden of AFI and to guide targeted interventions. While acknowledging the limitations inherent to retrospective designs and diagnostic constraints, this study emphasizes the global relevance of integrated surveillance in ecologically dynamic regions. Crucially, addressing these challenges requires improving data completeness, such as by the meticulous entry and digital optimization of GAL forms, to ensure accurate epidemiological tracking in complex equatorial settings.
full_text_sections.other: INTRODUCTIONManaging the prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of community-acquired acute febrile illness (AFI) constitutes a major public health challenge in Latin America due to its complex epidemiological profile and potentially profound social consequences 1 . A comprehensive understanding of their etiologies is essential for advancing clinical practice, guiding public health strategies, and informing policy development.The ecology of the Amazon basin—characterized by deforestation, flooding, and high vector diversity—creates favorable conditions for arboviruses and bacterial pathogens, amplifying the risk of febrile outbreaks 2 . Thus, the region experiences a wide spectrum of febrile illnesses caused by viral, bacterial, and parasitic agents, reflecting diverse ecological and climatic conditions 3 .The overlapping clinical manifestations of diseases such as dengue, malaria, leptospirosis, and rickettsial infections complicate accurate diagnosis. This diagnostic uncertainty often results in delayed or inappropriate treatment. Misdiagnosis may postpone life-saving antibiotic therapy, whereas indiscriminate prescribing contributes to antimicrobial resistance. The Pan American Health Organization 4 has emphasized antimicrobial resistance as a regional priority, highlighting its impact on healthcare costs and mortality.Community-acquired AFI contributes substantially to regional morbidity and mortality, considerably straining healthcare systems and requiring significant resource allocation for surveillance and management. Socioeconomic factors, including poverty and limited access to healthcare, exacerbate transmission dynamics and hinder effective disease control 5 .Surveillance represents a critical component of disease control. The Brazilian Amazon is recognized as a global hotspot for emerging viruses 2 . Integrated screening systems may serve as sentinel mechanisms for early detection. As deforestation and mining activities intensify, human populations increasingly encounter novel vectors such as mosquitoes and midges, underscoring the importance of screening febrile patients for malaria and arboviruses6. Without routine screening, outbreaks may remain undetected, manifesting themselves only as “unexplained fevers.”Amapa State, in the Eastern Brazilian Amazon, exemplifies one of the most complex diagnostic environments in the world. While dengue remains a major concern, the unique geography of the state—bordering French Guiana and the Atlantic Ocean, and dominated by dense rainforest and wetlands—heightens the risk of diverse infectious diseases. High rainfall and humidity render leptospirosis endemic, particularly in peri-urban areas such as Macapa and Santana 5 . Recent land-use transformations, including illegal mining and the expansion of acai production, have had measurable epidemiological consequences. These activities are consistently associated with increased malaria incidence due to favorable conditions for Anopheles vectors 6 . Moreover, the commercialization of acai has contributed to the emergence of foodborne transmission of Chagas disease 7 .EthicsThis study was approved by the institutional Research Ethics Committee (CAAE No 53153916.7.0000.0065). All data were anonymized prior to analysis, and access to secondary data from the Laboratory Environment Manager (GAL) and the Notifiable Diseases Information System (SINAN) was restricted to variables necessary for epidemiological characterization (with authorization from health surveillance authorities). EthicsThis study was approved by the institutional Research Ethics Committee (CAAE No 53153916.7.0000.0065). All data were anonymized prior to analysis, and access to secondary data from the Laboratory Environment Manager (GAL) and the Notifiable Diseases Information System (SINAN) was restricted to variables necessary for epidemiological characterization (with authorization from health surveillance authorities). Laboratory proceduresSpecimens were initially processed at the Central Public Health Laboratory of Amapa State (LACEN-AP) following routine diagnostic protocols, including arbovirus screening when clinically indicated. Additional tests, such as serology and polymerase chain reaction (PCR) for other pathogens, were performed at the discretion of attending physicians, with results recorded on GAL. Confirmatory local methods included enzyme linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) for immunoglobulin M (IgM) and NS1 (the latter exclusively for dengue), electrochemiluminescence, reverse transcription PCR (RT-PCR), and sequencing; for bacterial and fungal infections, ELISA for leptospirosis and blood, urine, and stool cultures were performed; whereas parasitic infections were confirmed using thick blood smears, the Strout test, electrochemiluminescence, and immunochromatographic tests.After initial processing, samples were stored at −20 °C and shipped to the Virology Laboratory of the Institute of Tropical Medicine of Sao Paulo, Faculty of Medicine, University of Sao Paulo (LV-IMT-FMUSP, LIM-52), in which they were preserved at −80 °C until further testing. Molecular screeningAt LV-IMT-FMUSP, samples underwent real-time PCR assays targeting viral agents. The screening included assays for Pan-Orthoflavivirus and Pan-Alphavirus. The following viral agents were tested: Flaviviruses, Alphaviruses, Orthobunyaviruses: yellow fever 8 , dengue, zika, chikungunya, mayaro, and oropouche viruses 9 .Genus Orthoflavivirus 10 : Japanese encephalitis, Russian spring-summer encephalitis, tick-borne encephalitis, Usutu, West Nile, and Saint Louis encephalitis viruses.Genus Alphavirus 11 : Ross River, O’nyong-nyong, Sindbis, Barmah Forest, Eastern equine encephalitis, Western equine encephalitis, and Venezuelan equine encephalitis viruses. Additional real-time PCR assays included pathogens with overlapping clinical presentations, such as enterovirus 12 , parvovirus B19 13 , hepatitis E virus (HEV) 14 , and Leptospira spp 15 . GALIn this study, diagnostic test results from LACEN-AP were retrieved via GAL.GAL, the national computerized system, was designed to manage and monitor laboratory routines within the National Public Health Laboratory Network. It is managed by the Ministry of Health via the General Coordination of Public Health Laboratories and tracks the flow of biological samples from collection to final diagnosis, standardizing results and providing real-time data for the surveillance of high-priority and compulsory notification diseases. SINANSINAN, the primary national surveillance database managed by the Brazilian Ministry of Health, is a decentralized system fed by the mandatory notification of diseases and conditions in the National Compulsory Notification List.SINAN provides high-resolution microdata (individual-level records) that include clinical and demographic variables (age, sex, pregnancy status, municipality of residence, reported condition, date of symptom onset, and clinical manifestations), diagnostic test results, among others. Integration of dataClinical and demographic variables (age, sex, municipality of residence, reported condition, date of symptom onset, and clinical manifestations) were combined with GAL laboratory results. Using this integrated dataset, data analysis was strictly descriptive, focusing on characterizing the reported cases.For the diagnostic tests either at LACEN or IMT, samples were classified as positive if they were reactive in at least one assay. title_original: Sentinel surveillance of acute febrile illness in a Brazilian Amazon region: laboratory findings and epidemiological implications

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to identify the potential etiologies of viral and other infections in acute febrile illness (AFI) cases reported from 2018 to 2022 in the Amazon region of Amapa State, Brazil, to better understand the epidemiological landscape of infectious diseases in the area.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was a sentinel surveillance conducted in public health laboratories in the Amazon region of Amapa State, Brazil, from 2018 to 2022. A total of 727 individuals were evaluated, with definitive diagnoses established in 185 cases (25.4%), including 23 cases of co-infection.
analysis.methods: Diagnostic tests included enzyme linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) for immunoglobulin M (IgM) and NS1, electrochemiluminescence, reverse transcription PCR (RT-PCR), and sequencing. Samples were stored at −20 °C and shipped to the Virology Laboratory of the Institute of Tropical Medicine of Sao Paulo (LV-IMT-FMUSP) for further testing, where real-time PCR assays were performed to identify viral agents.
analysis.main_results: Dengue virus was the most frequent diagnosis, accounting for 109 cases (16.8%) out of 650 tests. Other notable findings included leptospirosis (20/98; 20.4%), chikungunya (16/86; 18.6%), and measles (15/53; 28.3%). Non-dengue positive cases included Zika (9/62; 14.5%), parvovirus B19 (6/21; 28.6%), and bacterial infections (5/17; 29.4%).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted these findings as highlighting the significant role of dengue virus in the etiology of AFI in the region, with notable co-infections observed. This study provides novel insights into the distribution and prevalence of dengue and other pathogens in the Amazon region.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform targeted surveillance and diagnostic strategies for dengue and other co-infecting pathogens in the Amazon region, aiding in the development of more effective public health interventions.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's descriptive analysis may limit the depth of interpretation, and the use of multiple diagnostic methods could introduce variability. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the observational nature of the study and the potential for confounding factors.

analysis.summary_en: This study conducted sentinel surveillance of acute febrile illness (AFI) in the Amazon region of Amapa State, Brazil, from 2018 to 2022 to identify potential etiologies. Dengue virus was the most frequent diagnosis, accounting for 16.8% of cases, followed by leptospirosis, chikungunya, and measles. The study used a combination of serology, PCR, and sequencing methods to confirm diagnoses, with 209 positive results across 185 individuals. Co-infections were observed in 23 cases, and the results showed a moderate positive correlation with rainfall. The study's descriptive nature and reliance on multiple diagnostic methods limit the depth of interpretation, resulting in moderate evidence strength. These findings can inform targeted surveillance and diagnostic strategies for dengue and other pathogens in the region.

full_text: ABSTRACTFlooding can disrupt sanitation, contaminate water sources, and alter patterns of infectious disease; however, causal attribution of an individual febrile illness episode to flood exposure is difficult in retrospective hospital-based data. This study described hospitalized patients with acute febrile illness during a post-flood period in northern Vietnam, exploring associations with adverse short-term outcomes. This multicenter retrospective observational cohort included 237 consecutive patients admitted in Thai Nguyen province from October to November 2025. Demographic, documented environmental, clinical, laboratory, etiologic, and treatment data were obtained from medical records. Severe disease occurred in 8.4% and treatment non-response in 6.8% of patients. At admission, mean high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP) was 103.3 ± 98.3 mg/L, procalcitonin (PCT) was 6.7 ± 11.6 ng/mL, AST was 55.6 ± 61.4 U/L, ALT was 42.5 ± 46.2 U/L, and GGT was 79.9 ± 70.7 U/L. Recorded etiologic diagnoses most commonly included Escherichia coli (33.3%), Vibrio cholerae (18.1%), influenza viruses (13.5%), Leptospira species (11.0%), and Streptococcus pneumoniae (11.0%). Ceftriaxone was administered to 61.5% of patients. Separate univariable exploratory analyses associated severe-flood residence, non-clean water use, chronic disease history, hs-CRP > 100 mg/L, PCT > 2 ng/mL, and fever duration ≥ 3 days with adverse outcomes. These findings represent within-cohort associations among patients from flood-affected communities and do not indicate that flooding caused the illness episodes or outcomes. Most patients exhibited favorable short-term outcomes.KEYWORDS: Post-flood period, Acute febrile illness, Environmental exposure, Procalcitonin, C-reactive protein. MATERIALS AND METHODSStudy design and reporting guidelineThis multicenter retrospective observational cohort study described hospitalized patients with acute febrile illness during a post-flood period in Thai Nguyen province, Vietnam, from October to November 2025. The study evaluated demographic characteristics, documented environmental indicators, clinical and admission laboratory findings, recorded etiologic diagnoses, antibiotic utilization, disease severity, and treatment response. Reporting followed the Strengthening the Reporting of Observational Studies in Epidemiology (STROBE) guidelines. Supplementary Table S1 provides a complete checklist.Study settingPatients were recruited consecutively from Thai Nguyen Central Hospital, Hospital A, Thai Nguyen, and Thai Nguyen University of Medicine and Pharmacy Hospital. These hospitals provide inpatient care to communities affected by seasonal flooding in northern Vietnam. The study followed a major local flooding event with heterogeneous documented impacts, ranging from temporary water coverage to extensive inundation with disruption of care access and water-sanitation systems. No unaffected comparison group or independent event-level hydrological dataset was available.ParticipantsInclusion criteriaPatients aged ≥ 16 years; admitted with acute febrile illness, defined as a body temperature ≥ 38 °C; residing in an area documented as affected by the recent flood or with documented direct or indirect floodwater contact; and who had the demographic, environmental, clinical, and laboratory variables required for the planned analyses were eligible. These criteria defined a post-flood hospital cohort and did not establish that flooding caused the febrile illness.Exclusion criteriaPatients with incomplete records for the required analytic variables, fever clearly attributable to a non-infectious cause, or readmitted for the same illness episode during the study period were excluded. The final analytic cohort comprised 237 patients. The exact number initially screened, and the number excluded for each reason could not be reconstructed from the de-identified analytic files, which is acknowledged as a limitation.Data sources and variable definitionsData were extracted retrospectively from electronic medical records using a standardized case report form. Variables corresponded to the demographic, environmental, clinical, laboratory, etiologic, and treatment data summarized in Tables 1 to 4 and Figures 1 and 2. No missing values were imputed. Values presented as percentages; percentages may not sum to 100 due to rounding.Demographic and environmental variablesDemographic variables included sex, age, occupation, and treatment hospital. Age was grouped as < 20, 20-39, 40-59, and ≥ 60 years for descriptive analyses. Environmental indicators were obtained from medical-record documentation rather than independently verified geospatial or hydrological measurements. Residence was categorized as a mild-flood area when records described temporary water coverage without major disruption to care access or to essential services, and as a severely flood-affected area when records described extensive inundation with major disruption or contamination of local water and sanitation systems. Chronic disease history was defined as a physician-diagnosed condition documented before admission. full_text_sections.abstract: ABSTRACTFlooding can disrupt sanitation, contaminate water sources, and alter patterns of infectious disease; however, causal attribution of an individual febrile illness episode to flood exposure is difficult in retrospective hospital-based data. This study described hospitalized patients with acute febrile illness during a post-flood period in northern Vietnam, exploring associations with adverse short-term outcomes. This multicenter retrospective observational cohort included 237 consecutive patients admitted in Thai Nguyen province from October to November 2025. Demographic, documented environmental, clinical, laboratory, etiologic, and treatment data were obtained from medical records. Severe disease occurred in 8.4% and treatment non-response in 6.8% of patients. At admission, mean high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP) was 103.3 ± 98.3 mg/L, procalcitonin (PCT) was 6.7 ± 11.6 ng/mL, AST was 55.6 ± 61.4 U/L, ALT was 42.5 ± 46.2 U/L, and GGT was 79.9 ± 70.7 U/L. Recorded etiologic diagnoses most commonly included Escherichia coli (33.3%), Vibrio cholerae (18.1%), influenza viruses (13.5%), Leptospira species (11.0%), and Streptococcus pneumoniae (11.0%). Ceftriaxone was administered to 61.5% of patients. Separate univariable exploratory analyses associated severe-flood residence, non-clean water use, chronic disease history, hs-CRP > 100 mg/L, PCT > 2 ng/mL, and fever duration ≥ 3 days with adverse outcomes. These findings represent within-cohort associations among patients from flood-affected communities and do not indicate that flooding caused the illness episodes or outcomes. Most patients exhibited favorable short-term outcomes.KEYWORDS: Post-flood period, Acute febrile illness, Environmental exposure, Procalcitonin, C-reactive protein.

full_text_sections.results: RESULTSBaseline characteristicsOur analysis included a total of 237 patients hospitalized with acute febrile illness during the post-flood period. Most patients were male (65.0%) and were aged between 40-59 years (39.2%), followed by 20-39 years (34.2%). Most frequent occupational category was freelance work (28.7%). Most patients were treated at the Thai Nguyen Central Hospital (85.2%).Regarding documented environmental indicators, 157 patients (66.2%) resided in mild-flood areas and 80 (33.8%) in severely flood-affected areas. During flooding, 94 patients (39.7%) were classified as using non-clean water; after flooding, 89 (37.6%) were classified as using non-clean water. Maximum admission temperature was ≥ 39 °C in 120 patients (50.6%). Most participants had no documented chronic disease (93.2%). Overall, 20 cases (8.4%) were classified as severe and 217 (91.6%) as mild to moderate (Table 1).Treatment characteristics and outcomesMean treatment duration was 5.1 ± 3.2 days, and mean fever duration was 2.1 ± 1.9 days. Most patients responded to treatment (93.2%); only 6.8% did not respond (Table 1).Laboratory findingsAt admission, mean white blood cell count was 9.4 ± 4.2 ×109/L. Mean neutrophil percentage was 79.5 ± 15.1%, and mean lymphocyte percentage was 12.1 ± 10.7%. Mean hemoglobin level was 134.5 ± 17.3 g/L, and mean platelet count was 214.7 ± 82.2 ×109/L.All values in Table 2 were measured at hospital admission. Mean hs-CRP was 103.3 ± 98.3 mg/L and mean PCT was 6.7 ± 11.6 ng/mL. Mean AST, ALT, and GGT were 55.6 ± 61.4 U/L, 42.5 ± 46.2 U/L, and 79.9 ± 70.7 U/L, respectively. Mean creatinine was 103.1 ± 65.4 μmol/L and mean INR was 1.2 ± 0.1.Recorded infectious etiologiesRecorded etiologic diagnosis was available for all 237 patients. Escherichia coli accounted for 33.3% of recorded diagnoses, followed by Vibrio cholerae (18.1%), influenza viruses (13.5%), Leptospira species (11.0%), and Streptococcus pneumoniae (11.0%). Figure 1 shows the less frequent categories. Since testing was not standardized and the de-identified files did not consistently distinguish laboratory-confirmed from clinically assigned diagnoses, these percentages are descriptive categories from the medical record and should not be interpreted as pathogen prevalence estimates.Antibiotic utilization patternsCeftriaxone was the most frequently administered antibiotic (61.5%), followed by cefoxitin (8.4%), cefoperazone-sulbactam (5.9%), and cefuroxime (3.0%). Figure 2 shows the distribution of antibiotics administered to patients with acute febrile illness during the post-flood period.Exploratory associations with disease severitySeparate univariable analyses associated severe-flood residence with severe disease (OR 3.792, 95% CI 1.079-13.330; p = 0.027). Non-clean water use during flooding (OR 3.118, 95% CI 1.195-8.137; p = 0.015) and after flooding (OR 2.727, 95% CI 1.069-6.960; p = 0.030), chronic disease history (OR 8.059, 95% CI 2.983-21.771; p = 0.001), hs-CRP > 100 mg/L (OR 3.586, 95% CI 1.399-9.189; p = 0.005), PCT > 2 ng/mL (OR 5.623, 95% CI 2.082-15.187; p = 0.001), and fever duration ≥ 3 days (OR 7.923, 95% CI 3.022-20.773; p = 0.001) also correlated with severe disease. Male sex had an imprecise borderline estimate (OR 3.309, 95% CI 0.941-11.642; p = 0.050), whereas age and body temperature showed no association. full_text_sections.discussion: DISCUSSIONEnvironmental exposure and infectious spectrumWithin this flood-affected cohort, residence in a more severely affected area and documented non-clean water use were associated with adverse short-term outcomes. These internal exposure-gradient comparisons are not flood-versus-no-flood estimates and may reflect differences in comorbidity, healthcare access, illness severity at presentation, or other unmeasured factors. These findings therefore do not indicate that flood exposure caused the outcomes, despite correlating with established pathways by which contaminated water and disrupted sanitation can increase infectious hazards 18 - 21 . The heterogeneous recorded etiologic spectrum included enteric, respiratory, and zoonotic categories. However, test selection depended on clinical judgment, methods varied across hospitals and pathogens, and the records did not consistently distinguish laboratory-confirmed from clinically assigned diagnoses. The distribution presented in Figure 1 should therefore be interpreted as descriptive documentation within this hospital cohort rather than the true prevalence of etiologies after flooding 22 , 23 .Inflammatory biomarkers and disease severityMean PCT was 6.7 ± 11.6 ng/mL; PCT > 2 ng/mL was associated with severe disease and treatment non-response in univariable analyses. This threshold should not be used as a stand-alone diagnostic criterion, and the wide variability and limited event counts require cautious interpretation 24 - 27 . Mean hs-CRP was 103.3 ± 98.3 mg/L; hs-CRP > 100 mg/L was associated with both outcomes. These results are consistent with greater systemic inflammation among patients with worse short-term courses, but they do not suggest that hs-CRP or PCT independently determined progression. Larger prospective studies with prespecified adjustment are needed to evaluate incremental clinical utility 28 , 29 .Gastrointestinal and hepatic involvementMean AST, ALT, and GGT values were above typical reference ranges, suggesting the occurrence of biochemical liver abnormalities in some patients. Several infections represented in the cohort can involve the liver, but the study did not include systematic bilirubin measurements, imaging, adjudicated hepatic diagnoses, or longitudinal hepatic outcomes 30 - 33 .Mean INR was 1.2 ± 0.1, which does not suggest frequent marked coagulopathy at cohort level. As only summary laboratory values were available, the data cannot establish the frequency, cause, or clinical consequences of hepatic involvement 34 .Accordingly, the hepatic findings are descriptive and support routine clinical assessment when indicated, rather than a specific gastroenterological conclusion.Comorbidities and host vulnerabilityDocumented chronic disease was associated with severe disease and non-response in univariable analyses. This is biologically plausible, but sparse cells and the lack of multivariable adjustment mean that the magnitude of association may be influenced by age, baseline frailty, type of infection, or other confounders 35 , 36 .Fever duration and clinical progressionFever duration ≥ 3 days was associated with both outcomes. Prolonged fever may reflect delayed presentation, a more persistent infection, or other clinical differences. The retrospective design cannot distinguish these explanations or establish that earlier treatment would have changed outcomes 37 . Most patients exhibited favorable short-term outcomes. Ceftriaxone was the most frequently recorded antibiotic (61.5%) but indication, timing, microbiological appropriateness, and therapy changes were not evaluated. Its utilization pattern should therefore be interpreted descriptively and not as evidence of comparative effectiveness 38 .Sex differencesMale sex presented a borderline association with severe disease, but the CI included 1.0 and the estimate was based on few events. Possible behavioral or occupational explanations remain speculative and require prospective evaluation 39 .Clinical and public health implicationsThese findings support prospective evaluation of documented exposure indicators and admission biomarkers as components of post-flood triage. Such studies should use standardized exposure measures and diagnostic testing, prespecified multivariable models, and external validation. In the present cohort, water-source documentation and admission laboratory assessment were clinically informative descriptors but not validated prediction tools. At the public-health level, access to drinking water, sanitation, vaccination where appropriate, and vector and rodent control remain established priorities after flooding 40 . These general measures are supported by broader evidence rather than by causal estimates from this cohort.LimitationsThis study has several limitations. Its retrospective hospital-based design and requirement for complete analytic records may have introduced selection bias as the exact number of patients screened and excluded could not be reconstructed. All participants came from flood-affected communities, thus the environmental analyses were internal comparisons without a flood-naive baseline. Exposure classifications were based on medical-record documentation rather than independent objective measurements. Diagnostic testing was indication-driven, heterogeneous, and not uniformly coded as laboratory-confirmed, creating differential ascertainment and limiting the interpretation of Figure 1. Study sample was a fixed-period census without an a priori power calculation. Only 20 severe events and 16 non-response events occurred. As 20 univariable tests were performed without multiplicity correction and no multivariable analysis was undertaken, this study’s estimates may be unstable, confounded, and vulnerable to chance findings. Bilirubin, adjudicated hepatic outcomes, and long-term outcomes were unavailable. Finally, findings from Thai Nguyen may not generalize to settings with different populations, flood characteristics, diagnostic resources, or pathogen profiles.
full_text_sections.conclusion: CONCLUSIONSMost patients hospitalized with acute febrile illness during a post-flood period in northern Vietnam presented favorable short-term outcomes. Documented environmental indicators, chronic comorbidity, prolonged ever, hs-CRP, and PCT showed exploratory univariable associations with adverse outcomes in this cohort. These findings are descriptive and hypothesis-generating; they do not establish flood causation or independent prognostic effects.
full_text_sections.other: INTRODUCTIONFloods can contaminate water supplies, disrupt sanitation and healthcare access, and increase contact with environmental hazards, with important health consequences in low- and middle-income settings 1 - 3 . Acute febrile illness after flooding may include enteric, respiratory, vector-borne, and zoonotic infections 4 , 5 . A key evidence gap is the limited hospital-based description of clinical, laboratory, etiologic, and treatment patterns during post-flood periods in northern Vietnam. Temporal proximity to flooding does not establish causation for an individual illness episode; retrospective cohorts are better suited to describe patterns and generate hypotheses than to estimate a flood-attributable effect.Vietnam is vulnerable to recurrent storms and flooding. During the October-November 2025 study period, hospitals in Thai Nguyen served communities with documented temporary inundation and, in more severely affected areas, disruption of access and contamination of local water and sanitation systems. Quantitative hydrological measures for the event were not available in the medical records 6 - 8 .High-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP) and procalcitonin (PCT) are routinely available markers of systemic inflammation and infection severity 9 - 12 . Their role here was not to establish novel prognostic thresholds, but to examine whether routinely recorded markers revealed clinically relevant patterns in this post-flood hospital cohort.Environmental documentation, comorbidity, delayed presentation, and inflammatory response may be interrelated. Accordingly, analyses should distinguish the post-flood context from individual-level causal attribution and treat observed associations as potentially confounded and exploratory 13 - 17 .This study describes demographic, documented environmental, clinical, laboratory, recorded etiologic, and treatment characteristics of patients hospitalized with acute febrile illness during a post-flood period in Thai Nguyen province. Additionally, it explores univariable associations with short-term clinical outcomes. No causal effect or validated prediction model was intended.EthicsGiven the retrospective design and use of anonymized medical records, the requirement for informed consent was waived by the committee.
